chunks: My example among you is like that of a lamp in darkness; whoever enters it is illuminated by it. So listen, O people, and pay attention, and attend with the ears of your hearts so that you may understand.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of the lamp in the darkness used to explain in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali employs the metaphor of a lamp in darkness to illustrate his role as a beacon of divine guidance amidst the spiritual obscurity of his time. He urges the audience to not merely hear with their ears but to actively engage their 'ears of the heart' (*udhun al-qalb*), emphasizing the Shia emphasis on deep, contemplative understanding (*ta'ammul*) over superficial listening.
